text:
Zach Werenski won the Norris last season, and Evolving-Hockey had him fourth among defensemen at 3.8 wins above replacement, driving play at the 98th percentile. This season his name keeps showing up in a different kind of headline: Bleacher Report ranked him among players likely to request a trade next, and The Hockey News asked whether he's reconsidering his commitment to Columbus. Neither Werenski nor the team has said anything of the sort; it's speculation fed by a 0-5-0 skid.

His own season is quieter than the award. He has 16 points in 19 games after 81 last year, and his scoring rate is down from 2.44 points per 60 to 1.84. The team has also been lucky with him on, scoring 6.3 more goals than the chances deserve, so the points are if anything a little generous. Columbus takes 48% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there.

The shot is still busy (61 on goal, 41 blocks) and he still breaks the puck out cleanly: 70% of exits with possession in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. His ice time dipped to 19:30 in Tuesday's 5-1 loss, worth watching.
